scope.support: s.19(a) הכנסת רשאית, ברוב של חבריה, להביע אי-אמון לראש הממשלה; s.19(b) no confidence = dissolution; s.22 PM may dissolve the Knesset בהסכמת נשיא המדינה; s.52 Knesset oversight
scope.note: Checks altered, none removed or made inoperative: no confidence survives (61 MKs) but now triggers elections for both; removal of the PM without elections is replaced by ss.26–27 (majority after conviction; 80 MKs otherwise), each followed by special elections; s.20 budget default and s.58 continuing budget relax the budget lever with alternative mechanisms; new checks added: s.3(c) Knesset approval of ministers, s.35(c) removal of a minister by 70 MKs, s.48 committee approval of penal regulations, s.49 emergency declared by the Knesset, s.50(d) emergency regulations cannot bar access to courts, impose retroactive punishment or infringe human dignity, s.53 immunity from emergency regulations

temporary_provision.support: Permanent re-enactment replacing the 1968 law (s.61 חוק-יסוד: הממשלה – בטל); s.64 transitional provisions only

targets_judiciary.support: Subject is the executive and its relations with the Knesset; courts appear only as the PM's trial venue (s.25(b)), the bar on emergency regulations preventing פניה לערכאות (s.50(d)) and election appeals (s.62(6), new s.7C)
targets_judiciary.note: Not judicial review, judicial appointments or judicial independence

deviation_tier.support: s.19(b) הבעת אי-אמון ... יראוה כהחלטת הכנסת על התפזרותה; s.22(a) PM may dissolve the Knesset by order; s.20 budget default = dissolution; s.58 spending without a budget
deviation_tier.note: Principal subject: separation of powers (structure of the executive and its relationship to the Knesset). Values engaged: separation of powers, limited contradiction, since ss.19(b), 20, 22 and 58 shift leverage to the directly elected PM while ss.3(c), 35(c), 48, 49, 52, 53 strengthen the Knesset's checks; free and equal elections, entrenched (s.6 equal franchise for PM elections; s.13 majority with runoff; s.57 new s.9A; s.56 rigidity); rule of law, entrenched (ss.16(b)–18, 25–26, 43, 50(e), 53); core human rights, entrenched (s.50(d)); independent judiciary, marginal (s.50(d) access to courts). Contradiction takes precedence over entrenchment; a coder weighing the new Knesset checks as offsetting could code Entrenches

direction.support: Regime-structure law: direct election of the PM, formation, confidence, dissolution, removal, emergency powers; no provision on citizenship, minorities, women or the scope of judicial review
direction.note: Axes considered: Jewish identity vs equal citizenship, not engaged (s.6 gives the PM vote to all Knesset voters; s.62(10) ballots 'בעברית או בעברית ובערבית' is procedural); minority and women's rights, not engaged; judicial review/independence, not narrowed (s.50(d) preserves access to courts; s.25 fixes the PM's trial venue and panel). Coded from the principal subject, separation of powers, which is outside the three axes
